annotation.kind: direct formalization of Theorem 4.1 with fixed round-to-nearest Model-1 operations, the source algorithm, pre-theorem Section 4 estimates, and a pointwise second-order interpretation of lesssim

assumptions: The matrix dimensions m, n, and q and the word count p are positive.

The fixed input and accumulation formats satisfy Model 1: the accumulation precision and exponent range contain the input format, and both rounding maps return nearest representable values and satisfy (2.3)-(2.4) on their explicit no-overflow domains.

The diagonal row and column scaling factors are positive powers of two satisfying the maximal intervals (3.4a)-(3.4b), with factor 1 for a zero row or column, and every scaled element is bounded by theta=min(fmax,sqrt(Fmax/n)).

The p input words satisfy the complete input-rounded recurrences (4.29)-(4.30); the computed matrix retains exactly i+j<p, rounds every multiplication and addition of each retained inner product and every addition between retained word products in the accumulation format, and records no-overflow evidence for those operations.

The Section 4 derivation supplies the decompositions and zeta bounds (4.18)-(4.20), the retained/omitted partition needed to derive (4.21)-(4.25), the omitted-product estimate (4.26), the raw accumulation estimate (4.27), its count r and bound r<=np(p+1)/2, and the quadratic term in (4.28), but not the final bound or its collected coefficient.

NaNs and infinities are outside the finite-real model. Underflow is modeled; overflow is excluded on each represented operation; the target covers the paper's default round-to-nearest mode rather than the separately doubled directed-rounding variant.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p20_t3_multiword_forward_error {m n q p : Nat} (semantics : P20FirstOrderSemantics) : (for every fixed P20StaticMultiwordRun and its P20StaticSection4Derivation, p20FirstOrderLe semantics (p20StaticMultiwordForwardError run) (the four-term envelope (4.32))) and (the same forward-error relation with the range-free (4.33) envelope plus the two underflow envelopes) and (the input-rounding and input-underflow coefficients contain the displayed u^(p-1) factors)
formal_statement.plain_language: For every fixed round-to-nearest Model-1 execution of the scaled p-word algorithm, the source estimates through (4.27) imply the four-term first-order infinity-norm forward-error bound (4.32). The narrow-range envelope adds exactly the two underflow terms to (4.33), and both input terms exhibit the source's order-u^(p-1) reduction.

informal_proof: Derive the exact decomposition (4.21)-(4.25) from the matrix and retained-product decompositions. Apply submultiplicativity and repeated triangle inequalities, use both zeta bounds, (4.26), the raw (4.27) estimate and r<=np(p+1)/2, and bound max(a,b) by a+b to collect (4.32). Put zeta^2 and the two local omitted terms into one second-order remainder. Rewrite the same forward bound as the (4.33) envelope plus the two underflow envelopes and prove the two order-u^(p-1) factorizations by scalar algebra.
informal_statement: Theorem 4.1: the actual fixed round-to-nearest result of (4.29)-(4.31) satisfies (4.32), where lesssim hides the stated second-order terms. Equation (4.33) removes exactly the two underflow contributions, and the post-(4.33) discussion identifies the same order-u^(p-1) reduction in both input terms.
